Subject: Initial scope: org setup, invites, and API key provisioning

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for choosing Redwood. I'm your CS lead for the onboarding run; Monica (Implementation) is copied to own the execution. To get your first environment live we typically handle three small things up front:

1) Create the customer projects/namespaces you want us to seed (dev / staging / prod)
2) Seed an admin roster and service-account API key(s) for CI usage
3) Send user invites for initial admins (or wire SSO if you prefer)

Can you confirm:
- The exact admin emails you want invited now (or say if you want us to seed a single admin and you'll invite others)
- Whether you want us to provision short-lived service keys now or you prefer SSO first
- Any project naming convention we should follow (we default to novacorp-dev / novacorp-staging / novacorp-prod)

I've attached a short scope doc (onboarding_scope_v1.docx) that outlines the typical 1-week activation sprint and required inputs. If you can reply with the admin list and a preferred date/time for a 30-min kick (we have slots today and Monday), Monica will coordinate the technical steps and Karthik will handle the API provisioning.

Thanks — looking forward to getting you up and running.

Best,

Hannah Schmitt
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
email: hannah@redwood.com

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the quick answers. I can handle the API key and project seeding; below is our standard minimal permission set and the steps we'll follow unless you ask us to change them.

Planned actions (will perform after you confirm the 3 admin emails and give the green light):
1) Create three projects: novacorp-dev, novacorp-stg, novacorp-prod (as requested)
2) Seed an internal service-account per-project named redwood-service-novacorp with the following roles:
   - inference.invoke (can submit generation and embedding requests)
   - project.viewer (read-only to config and logs for tracing)
   - secrets.fetch (only for retrieving runtime credentials scoped to that service-account)
   Note: we will NOT assign org.admin or billing roles.
3) Generate two API keys for the dev project: one short-lived (30d) for CICD, one long-lived (rotation recommended) for manual testing.
4) Send invites to the three admin emails for project-admin role (can manage users and routing within the project).

Operational notes and safety:
- Keys will be annotated with creation metadata and a recommended rotation schedule. We'll also add a KMS-wrapped envelope if you request it.
- If you later switch to SSO, we'll help migrate users and perform a key revocation runbook.

Attached are the seeding artifacts I use for the process: service-account-template.csv (format for bulk service-account creation) and tenant-init-checklist.pdf (checklist we'll run live on the kickoff call).

If your 3:30pm PT slot works, I can execute steps 1–3 immediately after the call and send the generated key metadata to the designated admins over a secure channel (DocuSign-style link or our console ephemeral view). If you'd prefer we only prepare and not seed keys until you've received them yourself, say the word.

Command snippet (example)
$ curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/projects/novacorp-dev/service_accounts \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <ops-token>" \
  -d '{"name":"redwood-service-novacorp","roles":["inference.invoke","project.viewer","secrets.fetch"]}'

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Implementation Lead | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Attachment: service-account-template.csv (2KB, csv); tenant-init-checklist.pdf (14KB, pdf)
